sources: dossier=Required behaviors: 'sensor as a service kind' (2026-05-15, data-platform-extensions, artifact-only) and 'the four bundled sensors ... ship as deployable artifacts' (2026-05-17, sensor-messaging-unification, artifact-only); doc=service.md:19 (pre-edit) sibling-protocol enumeration listed executor/claim-producer/lifecycle-subscriber/blob-backend only, omitting publisher, though Adjacent already cited concept:publisher separately; code=ProtocolPublisher constant (claim_producers.go:52) parsed on equal footing with ProtocolExecutor/ProtocolClaimProducer; design corpus=publisher.md calls publisher a peer-service 'in the same trust perimeter as executors and claim-producers' with its own protocol, and conformance.md ships a dedicated publisher-protocol conformance subcommand.
note: Publisher is a real, code-backed, design-corpus-corroborated service protocol on par with executor/claim-producer/lifecycle-subscriber. Added concept:publisher to the line-19 sibling-protocol enumeration.

sources: dossier=silent on blob-backend's categorization as a 'service protocol'; Net position bullet 1 defines a service as 'an out-of-process gRPC binary implementing one or more rimsky service protocols'; doc=service.md:19/41 groups blob-backend with executor/claim-producer/lifecycle-subscriber/publisher as a 'specific service protocol' sibling concept; blob-backend.md never uses protocol/peer/dispatch/handshake/registry language and its own Adjacent list is attribute/inertness/persistence-database, not the service-protocol siblings; code=no ProtocolBlobBackend constant exists anywhere (only ProtocolClaimProducer/ProtocolExecutor/ProtocolPublisher and claimproducer.ProtocolLifecycleSubscriber) — blob-backend is selected via a distinct single backend-name config field, never a protocol-membership list, and never runs out-of-process.
note: Design-call for a human: should blob-backend keep its place in concept:service's sibling-protocol enumeration and Boundaries/Adjacent (as a config-selected pluggable backend that happens to ship a conformance suite), or be excised from the protocol list entirely, given it has no protocol-membership constant, never runs out-of-process, and its own concept doc never uses protocol/peer/dispatch language — unlike the dossier's out-of-process-gRPC-binary definition of service? Left service.md's blob-backend references as-is pending that ruling; only narrowed the false conformance-invariant claim (row 565).

sources: dossier=silent on the specific conformance-coverage claim, but Required behaviors frames conformance per-protocol via distinct subcommands, not a uniform guarantee; doc=service.md:32 (pre-edit) claimed conformance 'runs against the standalone gRPC surface each bundled service still exposes' and that a passing standalone run 'guarantees the in-process handler's semantics too' for all four listed protocols; design corpus=conformance.md: 'LifecycleSubscriber has no dedicated conformance subcommand; its idempotency is enforced server-side ... exercised by integration tests' and 'Blob-backend conformance via in-process construction ... adapts each concrete backend ... to the conformance library's reduced backend interface' with no standalone gRPC surface or image for either.
note: The invariant as written is false for 2 of the 4 enumerated protocols and directly contradicts concept:conformance. Narrowed the invariant to scope the standalone-gRPC-guarantees-in-process claim to executor and claim-producer, and added the accurate lifecycle-subscriber (no subcommand) and blob-backend (in-process construction, reduced interface, no standalone gRPC surface) facts in the same sentence group.

sources: dossier=silent on this specific cross-reference; doc=service.md:24 (pre-edit) pointed to concept:observability 'for the discovery-cache that consumes them'; design corpus=observability.md Boundaries: 'Does NOT own: the cache the handshake populates (see discovery-cache)'; discovery-cache.md Boundaries: 'Owns: the in-memory cache structure, the per-service entry shape, the registration-time consult path, the reachability status.'
note: observability.md explicitly disclaims cache ownership in favor of discovery-cache.md, so the pointer was wrong. Reworded the citation to send the handshake-mechanics reader to concept:observability and the cache reader to concept:discovery-cache (already present in Adjacent).

sources: dossier=n/a (prose-style rule, not a design-intent claim); doc=service.md:32 (pre-edit) read '...the standalone gRPC surface each bundled service still exposes...'; rule=ok-planner current-state-only convention (.ok-planner/CLAUDE.md, and CLAUDE.md's own citation of it) forbids temporal qualifiers ('previously', 'will be', 'still') in concept-doc prose.
note: 'still' is a residual temporal qualifier implying a prior state; removed it as part of the same-sentence rewrite applied for row 565.
